rubric.correct: Answer directly addresses the question; substantive visible claims match actual supplied frames, and unobserved measurements, contacts, completion, safety or clinical outcomes are appropriately qualified. A correct phase label alone is insufficient.
rubric.wrong: Answer contains a clear contradicted visual/evidence claim, an unsupported affirmative outcome/safety assertion, or a temporal reversal used to certify completion.
rubric.uncertain: Evidence is inadequate to decide a substantive affirmative claim or answer misses material requested limits. Explicit appropriate uncertainty is not itself a failure.
rubric.reference_conflict: Judge actual frozen pixels and chronology, not a reference pose that is absent from the latest frame. Record the conflict without rewriting reference IDs or awarding extra strict-ID passes.

limitations: One manual reviewer; no blinded independent second rater, clinical validation or calibrated general accuracy estimate.

All42 answers are judged correct for these supplied questions/frames. This does not mean every process step was completed, every stage was uniquely recognizable, or the app is appropriate for autonomous safety/clinical decisions.
Questions include guide/camera cues, and 32 stage labels remain a separate strict-ID measure. Correct answer semantics do not rewrite Guardian raw-ID scores.
Frozen inputs contain either eight or nine actual frames with recorded timestamps. Sparse sequences, edits, overlap and blur leave many completion criteria unknown.
The ten uncertainty questions test explicit scope limits, not all possible hazards or adversarial requests.
Lexical concept recall is a limited separate proxy and was not used to assign these semantic verdicts.
